headline: IML's Marc Whittaker flags Austal as a compelling takeover candidate trading at book value with a long US Navy order book and Aukus strategic relevance

Whittaker believes US prime defense contractors would be interested in acquiring Austal, particularly given its strategic role in the Aukus arrangement covering both submarine components in Western Australia and shipbuilding in Mobile, Alabama. We look at the Korean through Hanwha did approach the company some probably a couple of years ago now at levels below where it is today, mind you. But when you're trading a book value and you've got a great operating business and you're not paying anything for those operating earnings off that operating business, I think that makes you an ideal candidate... when you look at us, you look at the Aukus arrangement and the role that that Austal will play in that, whether it's on the submarine parts of WA, whether it's actually building the boats and the submarines in mobile, Alabama, where they're shipyard is, you know, this company is strategically well positioned, competitively well positioned.

headline: Prime Value maintains long-held position in Austal (ASB), citing $12.7bn order book, doubling revenues over 5 years, and net tangible assets 30% above current share price.
reasoning: Prime Value has held ASB for approximately 3 years with an average entry price of $2.30. Despite short-term headwinds including cost over-runs and government regulatory investigations of prior management, the fund sees compelling long-term value. ASB has won large, long-term US Navy contracts and received c. A$500m from the US government to build infrastructure it retains ownership of. It has also entered a heads of agreement with the Australian government to be Australia's shipbuilder of choice for a 20+ year, $20bn+ program. Net tangible assets at June 2025 are estimated at c. $4.40 per share, approximately 30% above the then-current share price of $3.40. The $12.7bn order book (including options) spans 14 vessel types with 10+ year duration, giving revenue visibility that supports expectations of revenues more than doubling over the next 5 years with earnings growing even faster from a low FY24 base.
quote: ASB has also entered a head of agreement with the Australian government to become Australia's shipbuilder of choice for a 20+ year program of shipbuilding. ASB estimates the volume of work at over $20bn over the 20+ years. The type of work undertaken for its customers varies from 'support' whereby repair and maintenance work is done on existing vessels to the construction of floating hospitals and modules for nuclear submarines. From an investment perspective, ASB has intangible value in the form of trusted relationships with government in the sensitive defence industry, established ship building capabilities and a skilled workforce. It also has hard assets in the form of inventory and strategically located land & buildings. After deducting liabilities, ASB's net tangible assets in June 2025 will be c. $4.40, c. 30% above the current share price of $3.40. We view asset backing as supporting the investment case and reducing downside risk, but more importantly it's the returns (nb cashflow) that are generated from these assets that drives the investment case. Future cashflows will come from its order book which is broad (14 vessel types), large at $12.7bn including options (with upside from the likes of the Australian agreement) and long duration at 10+ years. With the order book providing future visibility, we expect revenues to more than double over the next 5 years and earnings to increase much faster, from a low base in the FY24 year.

conviction: high conviction, held approximately 3 years, average entry price $2.30
